difference.candidate_requirement: Every report-trigger outbound queue operation must obey the bounded Redis command and HTTP request deadlines. If Redis remains half-open or stopped through the queue budget, return HTTP 200 with the exact per-delivery failure error=outbound queue unavailable, leave PostgreSQL, Redis, and Maildir unchanged, and permit an explicit retry after recovery without restarting the application or Redis process.
difference.oracle_behavior: After the real DMARC DNS discovery completes, frozen Java blocks the report request for the full twelve-second Redis SIGSTOP observation. It returns no response and commits no durable state until Redis resumes, then continues the original request and publishes successfully.
difference.candidate_behavior: Rust returns HTTP 200 with one failed DMARC email result and error=outbound queue unavailable while Redis remains stopped. It leaves source rows, outbound rows, Redis state, and Maildir unchanged, then accepts an explicit post-recovery retry whose publication matches the active seeded-delivery golden.
difference.reason: A half-open cache connection must not occupy an HTTP request or application task indefinitely. The rewrite requires hard dependency deadlines and bounded recovery, while preserving a retryable, non-partial outcome.
difference.scope: Only report email queue admission when Redis remains unavailable through the bounded queue deadline. Healthy queue admission, DNS order, generated DMARC bytes, successful HTTP bytes, Redis keys and TTL, Maildir MIME, source rows, application lifecycle, and short outages that recover inside the deadline remain strict compatibility requirements.

evidence.oracle_source_order: Frozen Java obtains the Redis task ID before message construction and Maildir persistence, then initializes Redis domain/task/index/pending state after writing the Sent file.
evidence.candidate_source_order: Rust obtains the Redis task ID before materialization, durably persists transactional queue/index/spool state plus an atomic Maildir write, and only then publishes the Redis projection; pre-admission Redis timeout therefore leaves no durable increment.
